stakeholders.name: National Oil Companies & Host Governments
stakeholders.description: NNPC (Nigeria), TotalEnergies Angola, and Petro Sudan are both partners and regulators. Production sharing agreements, local content requirements, and environmental bond obligations are all negotiated with host governments that have absolute veto power over operations.

engagement_tactics.option: Commit to local content hiring quotas above regulatory minimum
engagement_tactics.rationale: Builds political capital and social licence with the primary power holder

engagement_tactics.option: Challenge local content requirements in international arbitration
engagement_tactics.rationale: Destroys relationship with the entity that controls your operating licence

stakeholders.name: Niger Delta / Host Communities
stakeholders.description: Communities surrounding extraction zones have experienced pipeline vandalism, oil spills, and loss of fishing and farming livelihoods. The Nigeria Host Communities Development Trust (HCDT) gives communities legal rights to benefit-sharing under the 2021 Petroleum Industry Act.

engagement_tactics.option: Establish community development trusts with transparent fund governance
engagement_tactics.rationale: Required by the 2021 PIA; builds SLO and reduces sabotage risk

engagement_tactics.option: Rely on government security forces to protect infrastructure
engagement_tactics.rationale: Amplifies community grievances and triggers international NGO campaigns

stakeholders.name: IFC / Development Finance Institutions
stakeholders.description: The IFC, AfDB, and European Investment Bank provide project financing but apply IFC Performance Standards and Equator Principles as conditions. FPIC (Free, Prior and Informed Consent) from local communities is a pre-condition for disbursement.

engagement_tactics.option: Conduct IFC PS-aligned community consultation and FPIC process
engagement_tactics.rationale: Unlocks development finance and provides international ESG credibility

engagement_tactics.option: Use only commercial bank financing to avoid IFC conditions
engagement_tactics.rationale: Avoids standards but loses access to concessional development finance

stakeholders.name: International ESG Campaigners
stakeholders.description: Amnesty International, Global Witness, and Friends of the Earth monitor gas flaring, oil spill remediation, and human rights abuses in African extraction zones. Their reports directly influence institutional investor and consumer brand ratings.

engagement_tactics.option: End routine gas flaring and publish real-time spill disclosure
engagement_tactics.rationale: Removes the two most prominent campaign triggers

engagement_tactics.option: Issue legal notices against critical NGO publications
engagement_tactics.rationale: Amplifies international attention and reputational damage

stakeholders.name: Decommissioning & Environmental Regulators
stakeholders.description: DPR (Nigeria), NEMA, and country-specific environmental agencies are increasingly enforcing well decommissioning bonds and post-closure liability frameworks modelled on Norwegian standards. Stranded well liabilities can exceed initial capital costs.

engagement_tactics.option: Establish a decommissioning trust fund from first production revenues
engagement_tactics.rationale: Demonstrates long-term responsibility and reduces regulatory scrutiny

engagement_tactics.option: Defer decommissioning provisions to extend reported profits
engagement_tactics.rationale: Creates contingent liability and triggers regulatory enforcement
